question: What is the main purpose of priming extension tubing with normal saline before starting an IV?

options.A: To remove trapped air and prevent air embolisms
options.B: To warm the tubing up to body temperature
options.C: To test if the syringe plunger moves smoothly
options.D: To dilute any medication given later on

explanation: Clearing all air bubbles from the line stops air from entering the patient's bloodstream during cannulation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h3)

question: In the emergency stabilization framework used before transport, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bandaging
options.B: Brain
options.C: Bleeding
options.D: Breathing

explanation: Think of the trusty ABCDE framework! 'B' stands for Breathing, making sure air is moving properly into the lungs right after checking the airway.

question: What kind of items belong in the appendices of a research report?

options.A: The primary abstract and title page information
options.B: Bulky survey questionnaires, consent forms, and extra data tables
options.C: The main conclusions and nursing implications of the study
options.D: Personal opinions and reflections written by the lead researcher

explanation: Appendices keep your main text clean by holding large documents like questionnaires and extra charts out of the way.

question: In community health nursing, what are Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF) mainly used for?

options.A: Replacing clean drinking water supplies
options.B: Treating high blood pressure in adults
options.C: Treating severe acute malnutrition safely at home
options.D: Preserving fresh vegetables without refrigeration

explanation: RUTFs are nutrient-packed pastes that save lives by helping severely malnourished children recover right at home without needing a hospital bed.

question: A patient in her first trimester complains that her breasts feel heavy and sore. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: Early leakage of colostrum stretching the lactiferous ducts
options.B: Blockage of the lymphatic vessels inside the chest wall
options.C: Hormonal surges causing rapid tissue growth and increased blood flow
options.D: Infection of the milk ducts caused by elevated progesterone

explanation: That early tenderness is just the body's rapid way of gearing up! Hormones surge, blood flow increases, and the breast tissue starts growing rapidly.

question: Why do neoplastic cells form a tumor instead of behaving normally?

options.A: They expand rapidly because they are fighting off local infections
options.B: They grow larger to replace dead tissue in the organ
options.C: They absorb too much water from surrounding blood vessels
options.D: They multiply uncontrollably due to failed growth regulation

explanation: You've got this! Normally, our body tells cells when to rest and when to divide. In a tumor, those control signals fail, and the cells just keep multiplying without stopping.

question: During a Mental Status Examination, which section checks if a patient is seeing or hearing things that aren't there?

options.A: Perception
options.B: Thought content
options.C: General cognition
options.D: Motor speech

explanation: Perception assessment looks at our senses. It specifically helps you check for sensory disturbances like hallucinations (hearing or seeing things others don't) and illusions.

question: A nurse sees a public social media post from someone asking for medical advice about an open wound. What is the safest and most professional action?

options.A: Write a detailed treatment plan in the public comments section
options.B: Refrain from giving specific personal diagnoses and suggest they visit a clinic
options.C: Ignore the post and share pictures of the ward to cheer them up
options.D: Share the hospital's internal secure password with the commenter

explanation: Giving casual medical advice online creates legal liability and fails to provide safe, formal clinical assessment. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h7)

question: When should a sharps safety box be sealed and replaced?

options.A: At the end of every single shift
options.B: When it is about three-quarters full
options.C: Once a week regardless of its contents
options.D: When it is completely overflowing to the top

explanation: You've got it! Sealing it at three-quarters full stops needles from poking out the top and injuring someone.

question: When you add up all the percentages in a pie chart, what must they always equal?

options.A: The median value of the data
options.B: A maximum of 360 degrees
options.C: The total number of patients
options.D: Exactly 100 percent

explanation: Great job! Because a pie chart shows a complete whole, all the slices added together must always make 100 percent.

question: How do disaster preparedness drills and community workshops help with long-term recovery goals?

options.A: They replace the need for physical hospitals during emergencies.
options.B: They scare residents so they never leave their homes again.
options.C: They build community resilience and improve readiness for future crises.
options.D: They guarantee that natural disasters will stop happening.

explanation: Brilliant! Practicing through drills teaches both health workers and the public what to do, cutting down on panic and confusion when a real crisis hits.

question: As a community health nurse, you notice many toddlers are malnourished in a farming village. Which non-medical sector should you involve first?

options.A: Agriculture
options.B: Judiciary
options.C: Telecommunications
options.D: Transportation

explanation: Well done! Agriculture deals with food production and farming, making them our key partner in beating chronic malnutrition at its root.

question: Why don't modern hospitals just use simple boiling water to process surgical instruments?

options.A: It leaves a toxic chemical residue on the metal surface
options.B: It melts stainless steel components and plastic handles
options.C: It fails to reliably destroy bacterial endospores
options.D: It takes significantly longer than standard steam autoclaves

explanation: Boiling water is great for killing regular bacteria, but some hardy spores can survive 100°C. That's why we rely on autoclaves instead!

question: Which two common sexually transmitted infections are most often linked to blocked or damaged fallopian tubes?

options.A: Chlamydia and gonorrhea
options.B: Syphilis and human papillomavirus
options.C: Herpes simplex and trichomoniasis
options.D: HIV and hepatitis B virus

explanation: Spot on! These two bacterial infections love to travel upward into the reproductive tract and cause scarring. Knowing this helps you educate patients better!

question: Why are antiplatelet drugs like aspirin given to patients with peripheral artery disease?

options.A: To relax smooth muscle and widen veins instantly
options.B: To lower overall blood pressure
options.C: To dissolve large blood clots already stuck in deep veins
options.D: To keep platelets from sticking together and forming new clots

explanation: Platelets are the blood cells that clump together to form clots. Antiplatelet drugs make them 'slippery' so they don't form blockages in narrowed arteries.

question: Why is it smart for nurse managers to review staff feedback surveys about teamwork and collaboration?

options.A: To identify departmental friction points before they cause patient harm
options.B: To replace all human staff members with automated software
options.C: To decide which staff members deserve a pay cut
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future meetings

explanation: You got it! Surveys give the team a voice to point out where things are clashing, allowing managers to step in and fix things proactively.

question: Why are clinical supervision and peer support so important for nurses working in crisis settings?

options.A: They ensure that nurses never feel empathy for their patients
options.B: They are used primarily to penalize nurses who make charting errors
options.C: They help prevent burnout and address secondary trauma from exposure to crisis stories
options.D: They replace the need for formal psychiatric nursing education

explanation: You cannot pour from an empty cup! Supervision and peer debriefing give you a safe space to offload emotional stress and protect your own mental health.

question: What is a major workforce challenge currently facing the long-term care industry?

options.A: An overabundance of licensed nurses competing for very few open beds
options.B: Mandatory retirement ages that force nurses to leave the field early
options.C: Severe staff shortages and high burnout rates among nurses and aides
options.D: Strict laws prohibiting nurses from working in residential settings

explanation: It's no secret that long-term care can be tough. Low pay, heavy workloads, and physical demands mean keeping and recruiting enough nurses remains a major hurdle.

question: What blood pressure reading is used as the standard threshold to diagnose hypertension in pregnancy?

options.A: 130/85 mmHg or higher
options.B: 120/80 mmHg or higher
options.C: 160/100 mmHg or higher
options.D: 140/90 mmHg or higher

explanation: A reading of 140/90 mmHg or higher, confirmed on two separate occasions, defines pregnancy-induced hypertension. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h1)

question: What is a very common blood sugar issue caused by severe stress in critically ill patients?

options.A: Decreased metabolic demand
options.B: Rapid spontaneous weight loss
options.C: Stress-induced hyperglycemia
options.D: Severe chronic hypokalemia

explanation: When the body goes through severe stress or trauma, it releases hormones that often shoot blood sugar levels right up.

question: Why do we actually study nursing theories in school? What is their main job?

options.A: To dictate how much medication a patient should receive
options.B: To eliminate the need for doctor and nurse collaboration
options.C: To guide clinical practice and provide a scientific base
options.D: To replace hospital policies and procedure manuals

explanation: Think of nursing theories as the bedrock of our profession! They give us a clear, scientific reason for the way we care for patients every single day.

question: Which dietary habit is most likely to trigger a painful gout flare?

options.A: Consuming large amounts of fresh leafy green vegetables
options.B: Eating heavy portions of red meat and drinking beer
options.C: Using low-sodium table salt on regular home-cooked meals
options.D: Drinking several glasses of plain water throughout the day

explanation: You've got this! Red meat and alcohol (especially beer) are high in purines, which spike uric acid levels and make it harder for the kidneys to clear them.

question: Why would a doctor give a pregnant patient a tocolytic medication?

options.A: To provide effective pain relief during active labour
options.B: To induce rhythmic contractions for a post-dates labour
options.C: To temporarily halt premature uterine contractions
options.D: To prevent heavy bleeding immediately after delivery

explanation: Think of tocolytics as 'time-buys'—they relax the uterus to slow down early labor and give the baby more time to grow.

question: What is the primary medical goal when admitting a patient with hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Feeding the patient a heavy high-protein meal right away
options.B: Starting immediate surgical options to empty the uterus
options.C: Discharging the patient with herbal teas and rest
options.D: Correcting fluid and electrolyte imbalances with IV fluids

explanation: Before anything else, we must rehydrate and restore lost electrolytes to keep vital organs safe. You're thinking like a real ward nurse!

question: Why must a working defibrillator be kept close by during an EPS?

options.A: Dangerous heart rhythms are purposely triggered during the test
options.B: Sedation medications frequently cause permanent heart stoppage
options.C: The equipment is required to warm up the contrast dye
options.D: All patients suffer sudden cardiac arrest during catheter insertion

explanation: Because the doctors intentionally spark those weird rhythms to study them, the team must always be ready with a defibrillator just in case the heart needs help getting back to normal.

question: Why does the nervous system use electrical impulses for communication?

options.A: To store long-term memories in the blood
options.B: To provide rapid and specific responses to body changes
options.C: To produce hormones for the digestive tract
options.D: To filter waste products out of the brain

explanation: Electrical impulses allow the body to react almost immediately to internal and external stimuli, which is essential for survival. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h1)

question: How does psychoeducation benefit families of clients with mental health conditions?

options.A: It legally transfers all medical responsibility away from the healthcare team
options.B: It empowers them with knowledge about the illness and how to handle crises effectively
options.C: It completely eliminates all stressful events from their household
options.D: It teaches them how to diagnose and prescribe psychiatric drugs independently

explanation: When families understand the condition and recognize early warning signs, they can provide supportive care and prevent emergency situations. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h5)

question: A community refuses to use a newly drilled borehole because the water tastes different from their stream. What is the best IEC approach for a nurse to take?

options.A: Tell the villagers they are being stubborn and must use the borehole immediately.
options.B: Respect their concern, investigate the water safety, and explain the health benefits through dialogue.
options.C: Punish village leaders by withholding malaria medications from the local clinic.
options.D: Close the borehole permanently and force them to walk back to the stream.

explanation: Effective IEC involves listening to community concerns, validating their observations, and addressing them respectfully rather than using force. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h3)

question: What do we call learning to fear something simply by watching how other people react to it?

options.A: Reading a medical textbook about anxiety
options.B: Developing a fear directly from a physical injury
options.C: Learning to fear something by watching others react with fear
options.D: Inheriting a phobia gene from a grandparent

explanation: This is observational learning! If a child sees a parent scream at the sight of a lizard, the child might pick up that exact same fear just by watching.

question: A patient is having a full panic attack due to a phobia. What should be the nurse's very first priority?

options.A: Leave the patient alone so they can calm down in private
options.B: Force the patient to face the fear source immediately
options.C: Help the patient feel safe and lower immediate anxiety
options.D: Teach complex problem-solving skills during the peak of panic

explanation: When panic peaks, keep it simple. Stay calm, be present, and focus on helping them feel secure until the storm passes.

question: Long ago, during the demonological era, what did people generally believe caused mental illness?

options.A: Demonic possession and evil spirits
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiencies
options.C: Chemical imbalances in the brain
options.D: Hereditary genetic mutations

explanation: Before medical science grew, people didn't understand mental health issues yet, so they blamed unusual behaviors on spirits or supernatural forces. You've got this!

question: A patient starts having eclamptic seizures on the ward. What is your very first priority?

options.A: Ask family members to sign consent forms for blood transfusion
options.B: Ensure a clear airway and prepare to administer magnesium sulfate
options.C: Take the patient to the theater immediately for an emergency delivery
options.D: Collect a clean-catch urine sample to check for sugar and protein

explanation: Safety first! Always secure the airway during a seizure, and get magnesium sulfate ready—it's the gold standard drug for stopping eclamptic fits.

question: What is a major safety rule nurses must follow when a patient is in the lithotomy position?

options.A: Turning the patient every thirty minutes without fail
options.B: Padding the stirrups to protect nerves and blood vessels
options.C: Keeping the head of the bed elevated to 90 degrees
options.D: Removing all pillows from beneath the patient's head

explanation: Bare metal stirrups can pinch nerves and block blood flow in the legs. Always make sure those stirrups are well-padded!

question: Which of these common infections spreads mainly through direct skin-to-skin touch?

options.A: Scabies
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Tuberculosis
options.D: Tetanus

explanation: Scabies is caused by tiny mites that love to crawl from one person's skin straight onto another during close contact. Easy peasy!

question: Why does societal stigma directly harm the success of a sheltered workshop?

options.A: It causes the workshop building to physically collapse
options.B: It prevents nurses from administering oral medications
options.C: The public may refuse to buy products made by the clients
options.D: It forces workers to labor for twenty-four hours a day

explanation: Negative public attitudes make it hard to sell products, which hurts the financial survival of the workshop. You've got this!

question: A student nurse checks a drug's mechanism and possible side effects before giving it to a patient. Which historical role of nursing does this action reflect?

options.A: The nurse performing duties restricted only to senior physicians
options.B: The nurse relying solely on oral traditional folklore
options.C: The nurse acting as a primitive apothecary mixer from the Middle Ages
options.D: The nurse acting as an active safety barrier and clinical monitor

explanation: Modern nurses serve as the final safety check in medication administration, requiring them to understand drug actions and watch for adverse reactions before and after giving medication. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h6)

question: A clinic makes sure patients from all backgrounds receive the exact same high standard of treatment. Which quality dimension is this?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Efficiency
options.C: Timeliness
options.D: Effectiveness

explanation: Well done! Equity means fairness—ensuring every patient gets great, high-quality care regardless of their background, status, or wealth.

question: Why does the pregnant body develop normal insulin resistance during later gestation?

options.A: To protect maternal pancreatic beta cells from exhaustion and burnout
options.B: To encourage maternal fat storage for recovery after childbirth
options.C: To lower maternal blood pressure and prevent gestational hypertension
options.D: To ensure a steady supply of circulating glucose remains available for the fetus

explanation: Gestational insulin resistance makes maternal cells less sensitive to insulin, keeping more glucose in the blood so it can readily transfer across the placenta to the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h3)

question: What is a major spatial or geographical challenge for patients living in remote rural areas?

options.A: Long distances and poor roads making it difficult to reach health facilities
options.B: Too many doctors competing for patients in remote farming settlements
options.C: Excessive electricity supply causing medical equipment to overheat
options.D: An overabundance of specialized tertiary hospitals in small villages

explanation: That's right! Bad roads and long distances make traveling to a clinic a huge hurdle for rural residents.

question: What is an essential nursing responsibility before synovial fluid aspiration begins?

options.A: Drain the joint fluid independently at the bedside
options.B: Administer a general anesthesia to the patient
options.C: Perform a full surgical repair of the joint
options.D: Verify that informed consent has been signed

explanation: Because arthrocentesis is an invasive procedure, the nurse must ensure the patient understands the risks and has signed consent. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the main reason traditional healers make therapeutic cuts on the body?

options.A: To rub local herbal medicine into the body
options.B: To permanently change the person's facial shape
options.C: To remove unwanted body hair follicles
options.D: To test the pain tolerance of young children

explanation: That's right! These cuts help local remedies absorb directly into the skin or tissues for quicker healing according to traditional beliefs.

question: What is the main feature of a fixed cost in a hospital?

options.A: It changes directly with the number of admissions
options.B: It is always paid using foreign currency
options.C: It remains the same regardless of patient volume
options.D: It only applies to surgical ward supplies

explanation: Fixed costs stay steady month after month, whether your ward is completely empty or packed to the brim with admissions.

question: Why is it important to ask if a patient's joint pain started suddenly after an accident or came on slowly?

options.A: It helps differentiate between acute traumatic injuries and chronic degenerative diseases
options.B: It measures the patient's baseline daily fluid intake
options.C: It proves whether the patient requires emergency psychological counseling
options.D: It indicates the exact blood pressure medication the patient needs

explanation: You nailed it. Sudden pain usually points to trauma like a fall, while slow pain often means wear-and-tear or arthritis.

question: Which of the following best describes the multi-faceted role of a nurse working in a Nigerian primary health center?

options.A: Acting as a clinician, educator, manager, and community advocate
options.B: Writing laws and policies for the federal parliament
options.C: Performing complex heart surgeries in a private luxury suite
options.D: Working strictly as an accountant in a corporate bank office

explanation: PHC nurses handle diverse responsibilities, from treating patients and teaching families to managing clinic supplies and leading community health outreach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h10)

question: What best defines an accident in community health terms?

options.A: A planned medical procedure with complications
options.B: A chronic disease with a slow onset
options.C: An unexpected event causing injury or harm
options.D: An unavoidable natural health disaster

explanation: Accidents are sudden, unexpected events that cause physical harm or damage to individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h1)

question: What does antimicrobial resistance actually mean?

options.A: Immune systems destroying white blood cells
options.B: The human body rejecting prescribed vitamins
options.C: Microorganisms evolving to survive standard medications
options.D: Bacteria growing faster in cold temperatures

explanation: You've got this! Resistance simply means germs change and adapt so that drugs like antibiotics can no longer destroy them.

question: How does using the System of Profound Knowledge change how a nurse views a medication error on the ward?

options.A: It proves human error can be completely stopped if staff try harder.
options.B: It shifts focus from blaming the nurse to fixing flaws in the medication process.
options.C: It helps calculate the exact financial cost to the hospital.
options.D: It decides the best disciplinary action for the staff involved.

explanation: Great nursing management is all about fixing the system so humans can succeed, rather than pointing fingers when mistakes happen!

question: Which part of a draped instrument table is officially considered sterile?

options.A: The top surface and everything hanging below the edge
options.B: Only the flat top surface level with the table
options.C: The entire table including the legs and wheels
options.D: Only the center portion where heavy trays sit

explanation: Remember the golden rule: anything hanging below the tabletop edge is out of sight and out of the sterile zone!

question: As a nurse, why should you look at growth trends over time rather than just a single weight check?

options.A: A single measurement cannot show whether a teen is following their expected growth curve.
options.B: Single measurements are legally invalid for minors in healthcare settings.
options.C: Scales in clinics are rarely calibrated for adolescent body weights.
options.D: Weight changes too slowly to be measured during a routine annual checkup.

explanation: Spot on! Checking weight across multiple visits helps you spot sudden jumps or drops that might signal a health or nutrition issue.

question: How often should you check the skin where an oxygen mask and its straps rest?

options.A: Only when the patient complains of severe bleeding
options.B: Regularly during routine shifts and care checks
options.C: Only once a week before the patient is discharged
options.D: Never, because oxygen masks do not touch the skin

explanation: Checking the skin often helps you catch early redness and prevents pressure sores from the plastic edges and elastic bands.

question: How should a nurse approach dietary counselling with a patient?

options.A: An ongoing, continuous process
options.B: A purely administrative paperwork duty
options.C: A one-time hospital lecture
options.D: A task completed only upon discharge

explanation: Spot on! Nutrition is a journey, not a one-time lecture. We check in, encourage, and make adjustments as the patient heals. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h7)

question: Which joint works just like a door hinge, letting you bend and straighten your elbow?

options.A: Condyloid joint
options.B: Saddle joint
options.C: Hinge joint
options.D: Pivot joint

explanation: Spot on! Hinge joints (like your elbow and knee) move back and forth smoothly in just one main direction.

question: What is a crucial safety rule when caring for a patient in skeletal traction?

options.A: The patient's body weight must rest entirely on the traction pulleys
options.B: The hanging weights must remain completely unobstructed and free
options.C: The traction ropes should rest firmly against the bed frame
options.D: The weights should be placed on the floor to reduce tension

explanation: Those weights need to dangle freely in the air! If they touch the floor or bed, the pulling force stops working properly.

question: A patient's physical body parts and chromosomal makeup are best described as what?

options.A: Gender expression
options.B: Cultural role
options.C: Biological sex
options.D: Social identity

explanation: Chromosomes and physical anatomy define biological sex, which is different from socially learned gender roles. Spot on!

question: What is the big advantage of running a small pilot study first?

options.A: It helps identify design flaws before a large-scale trial
options.B: It guarantees that the main study will cost no money
options.C: It proves the research hypothesis is 100 percent true
options.D: It replaces the need for an institutional review board

explanation: Spot on! A pilot study is like a dress rehearsal; it lets us fix mistakes before spending big money on the main event.

question: Which process completely wipes out ALL microbial life, including tough bacterial spores?

options.A: Colonization
options.B: Antisepsis
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Disinfection

explanation: Sterilization is the highest level of cleaning. It doesn't just clean; it destroys even the toughest spores to keep surgical tools completely safe! [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a physical workplace hazard?

options.A: Repetitive wrist motion
options.B: Workplace bullying
options.C: Loud machinery noise
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: Physical hazards include environmental factors like noise, vibration, or extreme temperatures that can harm the body over time without direct chemical contact.

question: At which stage of the family life cycle do parents adjust to the birth of their first infant?

options.A: Childbearing family stage
options.B: Launching center stage
options.C: Beginning family stage
options.D: Aging family stage

explanation: The childbearing stage starts right when that first baby arrives, bringing brand new joys and sleepless nights!

question: Why is it important for a primary health care nurse in a rural Nigerian community to understand seasonal disease patterns?

options.A: To accurately predict the winner of upcoming local political elections
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of imported medical equipment
options.C: To schedule annual leave during the busiest months of the year
options.D: To anticipate outbreaks like meningitis or cholera and prepare preventive supplies early

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing when seasonal illnesses like meningitis or cholera peak helps clinics stock up and protect the community on time. You're thinking like a true nurse!

question: How is pharmacodynamics different from pharmacokinetics?

options.A: Pharmacodynamics measures drug absorption speed, whereas pharmacokinetics measures patient pulse rates
options.B: Pharmacodynamics only applies to herbal remedies, whereas pharmacokinetics applies to synthetic drugs
options.C: Pharmacodynamics studies how liver enzymes break down pills, whereas pharmacokinetics studies tablet manufacturing
options.D: Pharmacodynamics focuses on drug action and cellular effects, whereas pharmacokinetics focuses on body processing like excretion

explanation: Awesome! Remember: Pharmacokinetics is what the *body* does to the drug, while pharmacodynamics is what the *drug* does to the body.

question: What is a key requirement for successful community health education?

options.A: Using complex medical terminology to ensure scientific accuracy
options.B: Adapting the teaching to the cultural context and literacy levels of the audience
options.C: Relying exclusively on written pamphlets without verbal explanations
options.D: Conducting all teaching sessions inside high-tech hospital seminar rooms

explanation: Teaching only works when your audience truly understands it. Always speak in a way that connects with their daily lives and culture!

question: What practice helps germs develop resistance to chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Allowing alcohol-based hand rubs to air-dry completely on the skin
options.B: Changing cleaning cloths and disinfecting solutions after every single room
options.C: Washing hands with soap and water after caring for every infectious patient
options.D: Using disinfectants at too weak a dilution or cutting down the required contact time

explanation: You nailed it! If a disinfectant is too weak or wiped away too early, the tougher germs survive and learn to resist the chemical over time.

question: Why is promoting homestead gardening a useful nursing strategy against distribution failures?

options.A: It guarantees that families will never need to buy water or soil
options.B: It completely replaces the need for community health clinics
options.C: It reduces a household's total reliance on fragile transport supply chains
options.D: It stops commercial farmers from growing cash crops for export

explanation: Growing food locally around the home provides an independent, reliable source of nutrition when transport systems break down. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h8)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to directly ask new mothers about leakage or pain during postnatal visits?

options.A: Hospital policy requires a written confession of any weakness
options.B: Postnatal hormones cause temporary memory loss regarding physical symptoms
options.C: Midwives are legally forbidden from physical examinations without questions first
options.D: Patients often feel embarrassed to bring up issues like leakage or pain on their own

explanation: Spot on! Many women suffer quietly because they think postpartum leaking is just 'normal now'. As nurses, we must gently check in on them.

question: A nurse makes a drug dosage mistake and now gets very nervous and avoids preparing intravenous medications. What is this behavior called?

options.A: Aggressive confrontation of peers
options.B: Intentional insubordination to management
options.C: Professional indifference and apathy
options.D: Hypervigilance and avoidance behavior

explanation: It's natural to want to run away from tasks that remind us of a painful mistake. Identifying this avoidance helps us address the fear rather than just hiding from it.

question: As a nurse, what is the most important check you must do before giving a patient a new antibacterial drug?

options.A: Testing the patient's visual acuity
options.B: Weighing the patient on a digital scale
options.C: Checking the patient's allergy history
options.D: Measuring the patient's abdominal girth

explanation: Safety first! Always check for allergies so you don't trigger a severe, life-threatening reaction like anaphylaxis.

question: What is the main goal of public education in disaster prevention?

options.A: To ensure hospitals have enough beds during a crisis
options.B: To help communities build resilience and minimize harm
options.C: To take the place of professional emergency rescue teams
options.D: To completely clear out all natural hazards from a community

explanation: You've got this! Public education gives people practical tools to reduce risks and protect themselves before professional help arrives.

question: What is a major money-related barrier that often stops women from accessing healthcare?

options.A: Financial dependence due to lack of property and inheritance rights
options.B: Universal health insurance plans that exclude female patients
options.C: Mandatory employment taxes collected only from female workers
options.D: Higher hospital admission fees charged specifically for women

explanation: When cultural or legal rules prevent women from owning land or earning their own money, they have to rely completely on others, making medical bills nearly impossible to pay.

question: What is the main reason for doing a medication review during a home visit after a hospital discharge?

options.A: To throw away all old medications so the client can buy new ones
options.B: To let the family decide which pills the client should swallow
options.C: To increase the total number of daily prescription drugs
options.D: To compare hospital discharge orders with what the client is actually taking

explanation: Spot on! Medication reconciliation clears up any confusion so the client takes the exact right drugs safely.

question: You just gave an injection on a busy ward. What is your very next step with that used needle?

options.A: Recap the needle carefully and place it in the regular paper bin
options.B: Throw the syringe into the general black bin bag
options.C: Leave the syringe on the bedside table for the cleaning staff
options.D: Drop the uncovered needle directly into a rigid safety box

explanation: Never recap needles! Drop them straight into a puncture-proof safety box to protect yourself and others from accidental pokes.

question: When does a human baby first start picking up their normal body flora?

options.A: When solid foods are introduced
options.B: During the birth process
options.C: When the first adult teeth erupt
options.D: At puberty and hormonal shifts

explanation: Life's first big microbial exposure happens right at birth as the baby encounters microbes from the mother and the surrounding environment. Amazing how nature works!

question: What is the main goal of Intermittent Preventive Treatment in pregnancy (IPTp)?

options.A: To prevent the woman from ever being bitten by a mosquito
options.B: To boost the production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: To cure a severe case of cerebral malaria in the third trimester
options.D: To clear hidden parasites and protect the mother and baby

explanation: Spot on! IPTp is given during antenatal care to keep pregnant mums and their babies safe from the hidden dangers of malaria.

question: Which phase of a rescue operation involves sweeping the disaster area to find where victims are trapped?

options.A: Stabilization
options.B: Localization
options.C: Extrication
options.D: Evacuation

explanation: Think of localization as the mapping and finding stage. Teams use tools, dogs, and visual sweeps to spot exactly where trapped people are.

question: When you suspect a notifiable disease, what patient detail is MOST critical to record?

options.A: Patient's favorite food and dietary preferences
options.B: The brand of soap used in the patient's household
options.C: Patient's correct address and contact information
options.D: The specific color of the patient's bedsheets

explanation: Exactly! Public health officers need a correct address and phone number so they can find the patient and trace contacts fast.

question: Why must anticholinergic anti-spasmodics be strictly avoided in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma?

options.A: They paralyze the muscles that move the eyeball
options.B: They dry out the tear ducts completely
options.C: They cause permanent blindness within one hour
options.D: They can dangerously increase eye pressure

explanation: Anticholinergics affect how the eye drains fluid. In glaucoma patients, this can trigger a dangerous spike in pressure inside the eye.

question: Why do health teams run mobile clinics and community outreach programs?

options.A: To train people to become certified physicians
options.B: To reach populations living far from permanent health facilities
options.C: To replace traditional hospitals permanently
options.D: To collect taxes from rural farming communities

explanation: Correct! Mobile clinics bridge the gap by taking healthcare services right to the doorsteps of remote villages that lack permanent clinics.

question: How do State Health Insurance Agencies usually differ from the federal NHIA initiative?

options.A: They only provide care for surgical emergencies in private clinics
options.B: They prohibit civil servants from accessing any form of medical care
options.C: They focus heavily on covering informal sector workers and rural dwellers in their states
options.D: They are funded exclusively by grants from foreign international banks

explanation: You're getting it! While federal schemes started with government workers, state agencies make special efforts to reach traders, artisans, and rural villagers.

question: What is a common mistake when looking at a significant Chi-Square result?

options.A: Assuming statistical significance proves strong clinical importance
options.B: Expecting the sample size to decrease automatically
options.C: Believing that the expected frequencies must equal zero
options.D: Thinking the test can only be used with continuous numerical data

explanation: Good catch! A result can be statistically significant, but you still have to use clinical judgment to see if it makes a big real-world difference for patients.

question: How do second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics differ in receptor action from first-generation drugs?

options.A: They involve both dopamine and serotonin blockade
options.B: They only affect the endocrine system
options.C: They completely avoid binding to any dopamine receptors
options.D: They act exclusively as serotonin reuptake enhancers

explanation: Think of second-generation drugs as having a double action: they block both dopamine and serotonin receptors. This unique combination helps reduce side effects compared to older drugs.

question: Why must nurses alter health assessments across different life stages?

options.A: Hospital policies require a different form for every single year of life
options.B: Medical equipment only works properly on elderly patients
options.C: Adults do not need physical examinations like children do
options.D: Different age groups face distinct health risks and developmental needs

explanation: A newborn needs different checks than a teenager or an older adult because their bodies and life risks change over time. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main job of the human immune system?

options.A: To tell the difference between the body's own cells and foreign substances
options.B: To break down food and absorb nutrients
options.C: To filter liquid waste from the bloodstream
options.D: To pump oxygen-rich blood to body tissues

explanation: Think of the immune system as the body's security guard. Its core job is to recognize foreign invaders while making sure it leaves your body's own healthy tissues alone!

question: What is the primary goal of nursing management in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Working through staff and resources to meet patient care goals
options.B: Writing medical diagnoses for admitted patients
options.C: Handling hospital finance and billing exclusively
options.D: Conducting laboratory research on new medications

explanation: Nursing management focuses on organizing people and tools to deliver safe, effective patient care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is a common sign of compassion fatigue in disaster nurses?

options.A: Emotional numbness, irritability, and burnout
options.B: Increased energy and enthusiasm for work
options.C: Complete indifference to physical illnesses
options.D: An intense desire to work double shifts daily

explanation: Absorbing too much trauma without adequate recovery leads to emotional exhaustion and classic signs of burnout. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h8)

question: How does home care help the broader healthcare system?

options.A: By lowering the risk of hospital readmissions and easing ward congestion
options.B: By replacing all local clinics with mobile nursing stations
options.C: By ensuring hospitals never have to purchase medical equipment again
options.D: By transferring all medical debt collection duties to nurses

explanation: Managing chronic conditions and recovery at home keeps hospital beds open for acute emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of using unguarded industrial machinery?

options.A: Immediate trauma, cuts, or crushing injuries
options.B: Gradual chronic back pain
options.C: Slow onset of lung disease
options.D: Silent psychological burnout

explanation: Exposed moving parts on machines present an immediate physical danger, leading quickly to cuts, fractures, or even amputations if safety guards are missing.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent cross-contamination in the fridge?

options.A: Storing raw meat on the top shelf above fresh vegetables
options.B: Cleaning refrigerator shelves regularly with sanitizer
options.C: Keeping raw poultry separate from ready-to-eat salads
options.D: Using tightly sealed containers for all raw animal products

explanation: Never put raw meat on top! Juices can drip down onto your veggies, causing nasty contamination.

question: A patient says their cough has lasted 10 days despite taking store-bought cough medicine, and they now have a 39°C fever. What's your best nursing advice?

options.A: Stop taking all medications and wait another week at home.
options.B: Double the daily dose of the cough syrup for faster relief.
options.C: Switch to a stronger brand of cough medicine from the store.
options.D: Schedule an appointment with the healthcare provider to be evaluated.

explanation: A cough lasting over a week with a high fever could mean a secondary infection. It's time for a proper medical checkup!

question: Which task is classified as an Instrumental Activity of Daily Living (IADL)?

options.A: Controlling bladder elimination overnight
options.B: Bathing independently in a walk-in shower
options.C: Swallowing solid food during a mealtime
options.D: Managing household finances and paying bills

explanation: IADLs are complex tasks needed for living independently in the community, such as cooking, shopping, and handling money. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h4)

question: What does antimicrobial resistance mean?

options.A: The human immune system destroys all beneficial bacteria
options.B: Microbes change and survive treatment with standard medications
options.C: Antibiotics lose their expiration date while on the shelf
options.D: Patients develop an allergic reaction to powerful drugs

explanation: Resistance happens when germs mutate or adapt so that drugs that used to kill them no longer work. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why are open-ended questions preferred over closed questions when taking a dietary history?

options.A: They encourage the patient to share more details about their actual habits.
options.B: They allow the nurse to finish the consultation without speaking.
options.C: They take much less time to complete during busy clinic shifts.
options.D: They legally protect the hospital from documentation errors.

explanation: Open-ended questions prevent patients from giving simple yes or no answers, revealing more accurate information about their true diet. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient starts bleeding heavily right after birth?

options.A: Massage the uterus and call for emergency assistance
options.B: Wait for laboratory results before taking any action
options.C: Send the patient home to rest in bed
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward

explanation: Act fast! Massaging the uterus makes it clamp down and stop the bleeding, while shouting for help brings your team running.

question: Which type of nutrient is especially important for the baby's brain and nervous system growth?

options.A: Water
options.B: Fats
options.C: Starch
options.D: Fiber

explanation: Healthy dietary fats are superstars here! They provide essential fatty acids that build brain tissue and support your baby's developing nervous system.

question: Why do airborne diseases require special negative-pressure rooms while droplet diseases do not?

options.A: Airborne particles stay suspended in the air and travel much farther
options.B: Droplet nuclei are too large to pass through standard hospital doors
options.C: Airborne pathogens only survive inside the human bloodstream
options.D: Droplet particles are heavy and require direct physical contact to spread

explanation: Tiny airborne nuclei float on air currents across rooms, whereas heavy droplets quickly drop to the ground within a short distance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h4)

question: What is the main goal of quality assurance in nursing?

options.A: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment
options.B: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors
options.C: Preventing mistakes and monitoring care delivery
options.D: Increasing the number of daily patient admissions

explanation: You've got this! Quality assurance is all about being proactive—catching issues early and stopping harm before it even reaches the patient. Great nursing is about prevention!

question: A disaster survivor visits the clinic three months after a flood complaining of sudden nightmares, severe jumpiness, and avoiding the riverbank entirely. What condition is most likely?

options.A: Normal adjustment reaction
options.B: Bipolar manic episode
options.C: Acute Stress Disorder
options.D: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder

explanation: Flashbacks, avoidance, and hyperarousal lasting months after the traumatic event point directly toward PTSD. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h3)

question: When is traditional handwashing with soap and water required instead of an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When the patient has a known allergy to clear water
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.C: Whenever the nurse enters a patient's private room
options.D: At the beginning and end of every single nursing shift

explanation: Alcohol rubs cannot remove heavy organic material or certain spore-forming germs, so visible dirt requires physical washing with soap and water. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you must do before putting on examination gloves?

options.A: Open the outer wrapper
options.B: Perform hand hygiene
options.C: Check the patient's skin
options.D: Wipe down your work table

explanation: Always clean your hands first! Putting gloves on unwashed hands traps germs right against your skin.

question: Which symptom is completely normal and expected after taking misoprostol?

options.A: Permanent cessation of all menstrual cycles
options.B: Immediate high fever lasting for several days
options.C: Temporary nausea, chills, or mild diarrhea
options.D: Complete numbness in the lower extremities

explanation: Don't panic if a patient experiences mild chills or tummy upset—these are common side effects of misoprostol that pass quickly.

question: A baby with severe diarrhea is too weak to drink and shows signs of severe dehydration. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Administer high-dose antidiarrheal syrup
options.B: Start emergency intravenous fluid resuscitation
options.C: Wait for laboratory stool culture results
options.D: Send the child home with oral rehydration packets

explanation: When a child is too weak to drink and dangerously dehydrated, rush IV fluids are needed immediately to save their life. You are learning critical emergency steps!

question: Which type of safety intervention is generally considered the most effective at preventing future errors?

options.A: Holding a 10-minute verbal lecture during morning shift handover
options.B: Strong system changes like automated hard-stops or redesigning equipment layouts
options.C: Asking staff to memorize a new policy document binder
options.D: Sending out a mandatory email warning staff to be more careful

explanation: Forced functions and system redesigns rely on technology or environment rather than human memory, making them much more reliable. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h8)

question: Why is skin turgor checked over the clavicle or forearm during a physical assessment?

options.A: To evaluate the patient's overall hydration status
options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure in the upper body
options.C: To check for localized muscle weakness under the skin
options.D: To determine if the patient has a superficial fungal infection

explanation: Skin turgor reflects how quickly the skin returns to its normal flat position, which helps nurses estimate body fluid volume and hydration. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is an important duty for a community health nurse visiting a family with a physically disabled member?

options.A: Providing legal representation in court for disability benefits
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of local community health clinics
options.C: Performing complex orthopedic surgeries within the home environment
options.D: Conducting household assessments and teaching proper transfer techniques

explanation: Home safety checks and teaching family members safe transfer moves keep both the patient and the caregiver safe from injury. Wonderful practice!

question: What happens inside the eye when a person reads a book held close to their face?

options.A: The cornea changes its physical shape to bend light
options.B: The ciliary muscles relax and the lens flattens out
options.C: The suspensory ligaments tighten and stretch the lens
options.D: The ciliary muscles contract and the lens becomes rounder

explanation: Think of it like a camera lens zooming in: for near vision, the ciliary muscle contracts, which loosens the ligaments and lets the elastic lens bulge rounder. You're mastering this step by step!

question: Why should you always teach your patients the difference between a normal side effect and a dangerous adverse reaction?

options.A: It prevents panic over normal symptoms while ensuring prompt reporting of dangerous signs
options.B: It eliminates the need for any follow-up visits with the primary doctor
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience any drug discomfort
options.D: It allows the patient to legally prescribe their own antidote medications

explanation: Mild drowsiness is okay, but throat swelling is an emergency! Teaching the difference keeps patients calm and safe.

question: In the early days following Nightingale's work, what was the main focus of nursing studies?

options.A: Advanced surgical interventions
options.B: Pharmaceutical drug development
options.C: Hospital financial management
options.D: Nursing education and training methods

explanation: Spot on! Before diving heavily into clinical care, early nurse researchers first wanted to figure out the best ways to train and educate nurses.

question: Why do community health nurses need to adjust their standard routines during village outreach?

options.A: Government policies prohibit giving injections outside of clinics
options.B: Field conditions and local environments vary greatly compared to hospitals
options.C: Community members refuse standard hospital documentation forms
options.D: Vaccines given outdoors lose their chemical composition entirely

explanation: Outreach doesn't have the fancy setup of a hospital ward, so nurses get creative to keep things safe and sterile outside!

question: What is a major challenge for nursing students facing heavy financial stress?

options.A: Elimination of the need to purchase nursing textbooks
options.B: An immediate increase in clinical ward placement scores
options.C: Free access to high-end medical simulation software
options.D: Balancing exhausting work schedules with studies, leaving little time for rest

explanation: Financial pressure often forces students to hustle outside of school, cutting deeply into study and recovery time. Hang in there—balancing nursing school is no small feat!

question: Why is it smart for community health nurses to work with local market leaders when promoting food hygiene?

options.A: It stops people from selling food altogether
options.B: It guarantees that the local market will receive government funding
options.C: It helps ensure the hygiene messages are accepted and practiced by vendors
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid visiting the market stalls personally

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Market leaders are respected, so getting them on board makes food vendors much more willing to listen and adopt safe habits.

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: To promote positive and healthy behaviour choices
options.B: To replace modern medicine with traditional remedies
options.C: To distribute free medical equipment to hospitals
options.D: To punish communities that ignore health guidelines

explanation: Spot on! BCC is all about working together with individuals and communities to help them build healthier lifestyle habits.

question: What does 'reliability' mean when talking about a data collection tool in a hospital?

options.A: The tool gives consistent results when used repeatedly by different staff.
options.B: The tool can be completed by patients without any assistance.
options.C: The tool is legally approved by the national nursing council.
options.D: The tool measures only financial expenses rather than clinical care.

explanation: Reliability simply means consistency! If different nurses use the tool and get the same dependable results, it's reliable.

question: Why do nurses need to be extra careful with the membranous segment of the male urethra during catheter insertion?

options.A: It is the narrowest and least stretchable part, making it prone to injury.
options.B: It expands dramatically to hold large volumes of urine before release.
options.C: It is filled with sensitive nerve endings that cause severe pain.
options.D: It sits right outside the body where infection enters easily.

explanation: Good clinical awareness! Because this section is narrow and less flexible, gentle handling and correct technique are key when passing a catheter.

question: Why is finding immunization defaulters so important for a community?

options.A: It proves that community health workers are working hard
options.B: It helps health clinics earn more money from the government
options.C: It stops dangerous disease outbreaks by closing immunity gaps
options.D: It reduces the total number of children born each year

explanation: When children miss their shots, community immunity drops, making it easy for deadly infections to spread quickly among vulnerable infants. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h1)

question: In disaster management, what exactly is a hazard?

options.A: The physical injury sustained by a patient during a sudden road traffic crash
options.B: The total financial loss suffered by a community after a major flood
options.C: A dangerous condition, substance, or activity that has the potential to cause harm
options.D: An official government document outlining hospital shift rosters during a strike

explanation: A hazard is the underlying threat itself (like a flooded river or loose electrical wire), while the actual disaster is the terrible event that happens when it strikes!

question: What is the primary trigger for hypovolemic shock?

options.A: An infection spreading through the bloodstream
options.B: A rapid drop in circulating blood volume
options.C: An acute blockage in the coronary arteries
options.D: A sudden spike in blood pressure

explanation: Hypovolemic shock happens when the body loses a massive amount of fluid or blood, leaving the circulatory system with too little volume to fill the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of an institutional barrier to immunization?

options.A: Long distance between the remote village and the health post
options.B: Rude behavior from clinic staff and long waiting times
options.C: Lack of money to pay for transport to the health center
options.D: Cultural rumors regarding the safety of modern medicines

explanation: Institutional barriers come from right inside the health facility itself, such as poor staff attitudes or disorganized clinic flow.

question: Which of these options is a classic example of a traumatic emergency?

options.A: A bone fracture and heavy bleeding following a motor crash
options.B: A sudden stroke caused by a blocked blood vessel in the brain
options.C: A severe asthma attack triggered by dust in the ward
options.D: A sudden drop in blood sugar leading to a diabetic coma

explanation: Trauma involves physical force from the outside world, such as a vehicle crash. Great job spotting the difference!

question: A nurse assesses a wound and notes it as 'mild, moderate, or severe'. What scale of measurement is this?

options.A: Ratio scale
options.B: Nominal scale
options.C: Interval scale
options.D: Ordinal scale

explanation: Because the wound grades follow a clear rank order from best to worst, we call this an ordinal scale.

question: A patient is admitted with a ruptured appendix and severe abdominal rigidity. Which type of emergency is this?

options.A: Purely medical emergency
options.B: Psychiatric emergency
options.C: Surgical emergency
options.D: Non-urgent outpatient condition

explanation: A ruptured appendix is an acute abdominal event that requires immediate surgical operation to clean the abdomen and repair the organ. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h3)

question: What event finally tells the secondary oocyte to finish its second division?

options.A: Entry of a sperm cell
options.B: Degeneration of the corpus luteum
options.C: Arrival in the uterus
options.D: A drop in progesterone levels

explanation: Brilliant! The egg waits patiently in the fallopian tube, and the moment a sperm enters, it completes its final cell division.

question: What is the basic living unit of the human body?

options.A: Organ
options.B: Cell
options.C: Atom
options.D: Tissue

explanation: Cells are recognized as the smallest independent living units that make up all human tissues and organs. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: What type of computer is the bedside tablet you use for clinical charting?

options.A: Mainframe
options.B: Microcomputer
options.C: Supercomputer
options.D: Analog processor

explanation: Tablets, laptops, and desktop PCs are all types of microcomputers (or personal computers) built for everyday tasks.

question: What is the main job of our gastrointestinal (GI) tract?

options.A: Regulating body temperature and hormones
options.B: Pumping oxygenated blood to organs
options.C: Processing food and absorbing nutrients
options.D: Filtering waste products from the blood

explanation: Spot on! The GI tract's main assignment is to break down the food we eat, take in the good nutrients our body needs, and pass out the rest.

question: Which of these should you NOT do when teaching a community during an outbreak?

options.A: Using complex medical jargon to show professional superiority
options.B: Listening carefully to community fears and answering questions
options.C: Explaining simple preventive habits like handwashing clearly
options.D: Collaborating directly with respected local and religious leaders

explanation: Never use heavy grammar or jargon to intimidate patients! Always keep your health education simple, respectful, and easy to grasp.

question: Where is the pons located relative to the medulla oblongata?

options.A: Lateral
options.B: Inferior
options.C: Superior
options.D: Anterior

explanation: The pons sits directly above (superior to) the medulla oblongata on the brainstem. Think of it as stepping up one level!

question: What is a false social norm regarding adolescent sexual activity?

options.A: Believing that parents support early teenage marriage
options.B: Believing that all or most peers are sexually active when many are not
options.C: Thinking that schools provide too much health education
options.D: Assuming that condoms are effective at preventing all diseases

explanation: Teens frequently overestimate how many of their peers are having sex because of boasting, which makes them feel abnormal if they remain abstinent. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why is follow-up care considered essential for patients with chronic mental health conditions?

options.A: Patients no longer need family support once they leave the ward
options.B: Mental illnesses often require long-term monitoring to prevent symptom return
options.C: Community clinics have unlimited space for permanent admissions
options.D: Discharge medications are designed to cure the illness permanently

explanation: Because chronic mental health conditions fluctuate over time, ongoing care helps catch early changes before a full relapse occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is the frontline medication used to treat schistosomiasis?

options.A: Albendazole
options.B: Metronidazole
options.C: Praziquantel
options.D: Artemether

explanation: Praziquantel is the trusty, WHO-recommended drug used worldwide to clear up this infection. Bookmark this drug name—you'll see it often in exams!

question: What is the go-to, first-line drug recommended to prevent postpartum haemorrhage right after delivery?

options.A: Nifedipine
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Hydralazine
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: Oxytocin is our superstar drug here! It safely helps the uterus contract down firmly to keep heavy bleeding away.

question: Using the ROME mnemonic (Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal), how do pH and bicarbonate ($HCO_3^-$) move in a metabolic imbalance?

options.A: They move in opposite directions
options.B: They move in the same direction
options.C: They cancel each other out instantly
options.D: They remain completely unchanged

explanation: ROME helps us remember: in metabolic issues, the pH and bicarbonate are Equal (they move in the same direction—both go up or both go down). You've got this!

question: Which of the following is classified as a macromineral?

options.A: Iron
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Zinc
options.D: Iodine

explanation: Calcium is a macromineral because the body requires it in large amounts daily, primarily for bone health and muscle function. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h3)

question: Which specific Nigerian law is dedicated to protecting the rights and welfare of children?

options.A: The Public Health Safety Code
options.B: The Child Rights Act
options.C: The National Minimum Wage Act
options.D: The Land Use Decree

explanation: Keep this one handy! The Child Rights Act is the key legal backing we use to protect Nigerian children against abuse, exploitation, and early marriage.

question: Which group of people is most likely to experience thyroid disorders?

options.A: Having a high-stress occupation
options.B: Living in a rural farming community
options.C: Being female
options.D: Being over the age of seventy

explanation: That's correct! Women are diagnosed with thyroid issues much more often than men, so keep a close eye out during assessments.

question: How do adsorbent drugs help ease diarrhoea symptoms?

options.A: They bind to toxins and fluid on their surface
options.B: They increase blood flow to the intestinal lining
options.C: They paralyze the nerves of the large intestine
options.D: They stimulate the production of healthy gut bacteria

explanation: Think of adsorbents like a sponge in the gut—they grab onto bad toxins and extra liquid, carrying them safely out in the stool.

question: What is the main reason pregnant women are encouraged to attend routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.A: To provide the mother with high doses of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: To permanently prevent any potential complications during the postpartum period
options.C: To schedule the exact date and time when labor will officially begin
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for conditions like anemia and high blood pressure

explanation: ANC is like a check-point for safety! It helps midwives and nurses catch small issues like low blood levels or high BP early before they become emergencies.

question: Is the pH of normal semen acidic, neutral, or alkaline?

options.A: Slightly acidic
options.B: Extremely acidic
options.C: Alkaline
options.D: Neutral

explanation: Semen is alkaline, which acts like a protective shield against the naturally acidic environment inside the female reproductive tract.

question: Where is the best anatomical site to inject emergency epinephrine?

options.A: Gluteal muscle
options.B: Mid-outer thigh
options.C: Subcutaneous abdomen
options.D: Deltoid muscle

explanation: The vastus lateralis (mid-outer thigh) absorbs epinephrine the fastest into the bloodstream. Plus, you can even give it right through trousers in a rush!

question: A patient comes in with a severe pain crisis, but their oxygen saturation is completely normal at 98% on room air. What should you do about oxygen therapy?

options.A: Administer high-flow oxygen immediately to reverse the bone pain
options.B: Place the patient on a non-rebreather mask to prevent acute chest syndrome
options.C: Monitor saturation closely and withhold oxygen unless desaturation occurs
options.D: Apply nasal cannula oxygen only during periods of sleep

explanation: If their oxygen level is fine, extra oxygen isn't needed—in fact, it can trick the bone marrow into slowing down red blood cell production. Just keep a close eye on them!

question: When should a nurse document that a medication has been given?

options.A: Before going to prepare the medication in the treatment room
options.B: Immediately after administering the medication to the patient
options.C: Before checking the patient's identity band on the bed
options.D: At the end of the entire nursing shift for all patients combined

explanation: Documentation must happen right after giving the drug to prevent accidental double-dosing and maintain an accurate medical record. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which simple home modification helps a visually impaired person see the edges of stairs more easily?

options.A: Removing handrails to encourage independent balance
options.B: Polishing the wooden stairs until they shine brightly
options.C: Placing soft carpets over every single step
options.D: Applying high-contrast tape to the edge of each step

explanation: Using bright, high-contrast tape on stair edges makes each step stand out clearly, greatly reducing the risk of a nasty fall.

question: What is the number one risk factor for developing a placenta accreta?

options.A: A history of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Previous uterine surgery or cesarean section
options.C: Eating a high-fat diet during pregnancy
options.D: Advanced maternal age over 40 years

explanation: Past surgeries leave scar tissue in the uterus, making it easy for the placenta to grow way too deep during a future pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h4)

question: Which type of bedpan is best to use for a patient who has a broken hip?

options.A: A standard high-backed bedpan
options.B: A rigid plastic commode chair
options.C: A fracture pan
options.D: A pediatric incontinence ring

explanation: Fracture pans are shallow, meaning you don't have to lift the patient's hips high up. This is a lifesaver for avoiding extra pain or injury when dealing with hip or pelvic bones!

question: Which of these should you NOT do when planning a community health talk against harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Mocking and condemning traditional cultural heritage
options.B: Partnering with respected local village elders
options.C: Educating parents about blood-borne infection risks
options.D: Promoting safe, non-invasive alternatives for identity

explanation: Spot on! Insulting local culture only makes people defensive. Good public health education is always respectful, kind, and informative.

question: A researcher notices many patients stopped attending a 6-month weight loss study before it ended. What is this called?

options.A: The Hawthorne effect
options.B: A confounding variable
options.C: Attrition bias
options.D: Random assignment

explanation: You nailed it! 'Attrition' just means people dropping out over time, which can leave us with a lopsided group of results.

question: Which of these is considered a biological factor that affects a person's mental health?

options.A: Cultural beliefs regarding emotional expression
options.B: Genetic makeup and brain chemical balance
options.C: Family income level and daily wages
options.D: The availability of stable local housing

explanation: Biological factors are things hardwired into our bodies—like our genes and neurotransmitters—rather than outside social conditions like housing or money.

question: A nurse notices patients keep tripping in a dim hallway at night. What is the best first step for this nurse?

options.A: Ignore the issue because patient falls are an unavoidable part of hospitalization.
options.B: Wait for an annual hospital inspection to report the lighting issue.
options.C: Punish the night shift nursing assistants for not watching patients closely enough.
options.D: Identify the problem and participate in finding a practical solution like better night lighting.

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Nurses lead the way in quality improvement by spotting everyday hazards and helping to put simple, practical fixes in place.

question: Through which bone does smell nerve fibers pass to reach the brain?

options.A: Internal acoustic meatus of the temporal bone
options.B: Superior orbital fissure of the orbit
options.C: Cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone
options.D: Foramen magnum of the occipital bone

explanation: Spot on! Tiny nerve fibers pass upward through the tiny holes in the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to reach the brain's olfactory bulb. Fun anatomy fact to keep in mind!

question: Which objective of health education deals with building practical self-care skills like handwashing?

options.A: Cognitive objective
options.B: Affective objective
options.C: Psychodynamic objective
options.D: Administrative objective

explanation: The psychodynamic (or behavioral) objective focuses on the physical execution of practical skills—getting hands-on with procedures like wound care.

question: What is your main job as the nurse while the doctor performs a thoracentesis?

options.A: Reading the final lab results before fluid collection
options.B: Inserting the drainage catheter into the pleural cavity
options.C: Administering general anesthesia through an IV line
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and watching for signs of distress

explanation: Exactly right! Your eyes are on the patient—keep a close check on their breathing, heart rate, and comfort while the fluid drains.

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing an accurate baseline assessment upon ICU admission?

options.A: To provide a reference point for detecting future changes
options.B: To determine the exact discharge date
options.C: To eliminate the need for future vital sign checks
options.D: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements

explanation: You cannot spot an abnormal change if you do not know what the patient's normal starting point looked like when they arrived. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a pathway for lymphatic drainage from the uterus and ovaries?

options.A: Axillary lymph nodes
options.B: External iliac nodes
options.C: Internal iliac nodes
options.D: Lumbar lymph nodes

explanation: Axillary nodes drain the arms and breasts, not the deep pelvic reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of secondary stroke prevention strategies?

options.A: To prevent a recurrent stroke by managing underlying risk factors
options.B: To eliminate the need for any ongoing physical therapy
options.C: To reverse existing brain cell death and restore lost tissue
options.D: To cure the underlying genetic cause of high blood pressure

explanation: Brilliant! Secondary prevention is all about keeping lifestyle habits in check, taking medications properly, and managing blood pressure to stop another stroke from happening.

question: Why is gathering comprehensive baseline data essential at the very start of a prospective study?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any further follow-up appointments
options.B: It allows researchers to alter the inclusion criteria midway through the study
options.C: It establishes a clear, accurate starting point to compare against future changes
options.D: It guarantees that no participants will ever drop out of the project

explanation: Accurate baseline measurements are necessary to accurately measure how much change occurs over time in the subsequent follow-up phases. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of home care for family members?

options.A: They receive official nursing licenses after a single week of observation
options.B: They are completely relieved of any responsibility regarding the patient
options.C: They no longer need to pay for any household utility bills
options.D: They can learn practical care techniques while staying closely involved

explanation: Home care allows family members to participate directly in daily support and gain hands-on knowledge from the nurse. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why is post-abortion care viewed as a complete package rather than just a single medical procedure?

options.A: It must involve legal teams alongside medical doctors in every case
options.B: It requires multiple surgical operations over a span of several months
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, counseling, contraception, and health linkages
options.D: It is only performed in specialized tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Spot on! PAC covers more than just the immediate physical cleanup—it looks at the whole person by offering counseling, family planning, and follow-up support.

question: What is the main goal of a peer support program for second victims?

options.A: To find grounds for disciplinary action or termination
options.B: To re-test the nurse's clinical skills in a simulation lab
options.C: To conduct a legal investigation of the nurse's actions
options.D: To provide a confidential space to talk with trained colleagues

explanation: Sometimes you just need someone who truly understands the hospital ward stress to listen without judging. Peer support is all about healing together!

question: How can you best protect a patient's dignity and privacy when giving them a bed bath?

options.A: By keeping completely silent so they don't feel awkward
options.B: By asking all family members to stay outside forever
options.C: By opening the ward windows wide for fresh air
options.D: By keeping the patient covered with a sheet and exposing only the area being washed

explanation: Brilliant! Strategic draping with a bedsheet keeps your patient covered, warm, and feeling respected while you work.

question: How can a patient with severe upper body paralysis steer an automated wheelchair?

options.A: A heavy floor-based foot pedal
options.B: A sip-and-puff mechanism
options.C: A ceiling-mounted pull cord
options.D: A standard manual push rim

explanation: Brilliant! A sip-and-puff control lets patients steer simply by blowing into or inhaling through a small straw tube using breath pressure.

question: What misconception do people sometimes hold about money spent on health care?

options.A: They think it only benefits retired politicians
options.B: They view it as a waste rather than a productive investment
options.C: They assume it is managed entirely by foreign countries
options.D: They believe it always causes inflation in food prices

explanation: Many budget planners incorrectly see health as a cost center rather than recognizing that a healthy population drives economic growth. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which nervous system kicks in when a patient practices slow, deep breathing?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Somatic nervous system
options.C: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.D: Sympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing signals your vagus nerve to turn on the parasympathetic system—your body's wonderful 'rest-and-digest' mode that cools everything down.

question: Which two main blood vessel systems supply oxygenated blood to the brain?

options.A: Brachiocephalic and thoracic trunks
options.B: Coronary and pulmonary arteries
options.C: Internal carotid and vertebral arteries
options.D: Subclavian and jugular vessels

explanation: Great job! The internal carotid arteries supply the front of the brain, while the vertebral arteries supply the back. Together, they keep the brain well-nourished with oxygen.

question: Why do nurses need to know about parasitic ova?

options.A: To prescribe the correct surgical removal of adult worms
