options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure of infected patients
options.C: To synthesize new anti-parasitic medications in the lab
options.D: To help confirm parasite infections through lab results

explanation: Recognizing ova helps you read lab reports and understand how these little bugs cause trouble in patients. Great job!

question: Which measurement is most important for checking brain growth or fluid buildup in an infant?

options.A: Crown-to-heel length
options.B: Chest circumference
options.C: Mid-upper arm circumference
options.D: Head circumference

explanation: Great! Measuring head circumference routinely helps us monitor brain development and spot any abnormal swelling or fluid early.

question: In nursing, what is a 'fomite'?

options.A: An inanimate object that harbors germs
options.B: A chemical used to clean wounds
options.C: A type of resistant bacterium
options.D: An insect that carries disease

explanation: You nailed it! Fomites are non-living items like BP cuffs, tables, or stethoscopes that can pass germs from one person to another.

question: When does a pregnant woman's blood pressure usually drop to its lowest point?

options.A: During the second trimester
options.B: Right before active labour begins
options.C: During the first few weeks postpartum
options.D: Immediately after delivery

explanation: You got it! Vascular resistance drops around mid-pregnancy, bringing blood pressure down before it goes back up near term.

question: What control measure involves replacing a toxic chemical with a harmless water-based cleaner?

options.A: Engineering control
options.B: Administrative control
options.C: Elimination
options.D: Substitution

explanation: Think of 'substitution' like substituting a player on a football pitch—you take out the dangerous chemical and put in a safer one to do the same job!

question: A nurse throws an expired bottle of liquid antibiotic into the regular office dustbin. What type of sorting mistake happened here?

options.A: Infectious waste placed in pathological waste
options.B: Sharps waste placed in chemical waste containers
options.C: General waste placed in hazardous containment
options.D: Pharmaceutical waste placed in general waste

explanation: Medicines and drugs are pharmaceutical waste. They need special disposal methods and should never be mixed with everyday office trash.

question: What is the main purpose of post-administration monitoring after giving an oral drug?

options.A: To update the hospital kitchen about the patient's dietary intake
options.B: To clean the medication cup and return it to the storage room
options.C: To calculate how much money the patient owes for the prescription
options.D: To evaluate if the drug worked and watch for any adverse reactions

explanation: Monitoring ensures the medication produces the desired therapeutic outcome and allows the nurse to catch side effects or allergic reactions early. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign of superficial thrombophlebitis in a vulval vein?

options.A: A firm, tender, cord-like swelling in the tissue
options.B: Mild discomfort when walking or sitting down
options.C: Complete absence of any pain or tenderness
options.D: Localized redness and warmth over the vessel

explanation: When a vein gets inflamed and forms a little clot (thrombophlebitis), it hurts! There is never a 'complete absence' of pain—it's usually tender, warm, and swollen.

question: In the popular SOAP charting format, what does the letter 'O' stand for?

options.A: Optimal outcome
options.B: Objective data
options.C: Ongoing order
options.D: Observed opinion

explanation: You've got this! 'O' is for objective data—the things you can actually measure and see, like vital signs and physical exam results.

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a pregnant woman must report straight away?

options.A: Occasional mild heartburn
options.B: Decreased fetal movement
options.C: Increased fatigue in the evening
options.D: Mild swelling in the ankles

explanation: Always teach mums to track their baby's kicks! Fewer movements can mean the baby is stressed and needs an immediate check-up.

question: Which health history is a strict warning (contraindication) against using estrogen-based birth control?

options.A: Simple tension headaches
options.B: Mild seasonal pollen allergies
options.C: Well-controlled iron deficiency
options.D: History of deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Spot on! Estrogen can raise clotting risks, so giving it to someone with a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is unsafe. Always check patient history first!

question: Why is blunt heart injury often harder to spot right away compared to a stab wound?

options.A: X-ray machines cannot take pictures of blunt force trauma.
options.B: The chest wall often shows no open wounds or obvious external damage.
options.C: The heart stops beating completely right away.
options.D: Symptoms only appear several weeks after the accident.

explanation: Because the skin and ribs stay intact, there's no open wound to warn you. That's why nurses have to stay alert for hidden internal bruising!

question: Why is the issue of consent particularly critical when discussing forced marriage?

options.A: Consent is only relevant in urban healthcare settings
options.B: Minors and coerced individuals cannot give free and informed agreement
options.C: Adults over 18 never experience forced marriage situations
options.D: Legal documents require parental signatures for all marriages

explanation: True consent requires maturity, capacity, and freedom from pressure, elements that are absent when external forces dictate a union. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why might an expectant father develop physical symptoms like nausea or fatigue?

options.A: Because of direct hormonal exposure from the mother
options.B: As a somatic response to the stress and empathy of pregnancy
options.C: As a sign of an undiagnosed infectious disease
options.D: To manipulate attention away from the pregnant partner

explanation: Couvade symptoms show how deeply emotional connection can turn into real physical reactions for partners too!

question: A kitchen worker has a small healing cut on their finger. What should they do before handling food?

options.A: Cover it with a waterproof bandage and wear a clean glove
options.B: Apply palm oil to the cut to create a natural barrier against germs
options.C: Stay home for the entire week until the cut is fully closed
options.D: Wash the finger with cold water and continue working normally

explanation: Spot on! Open cuts carry lots of bacteria like Staphylococcus, so always seal them up with a waterproof cover and a glove.

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing practice when caring for a post-abortion patient with a weak immune system?

options.A: Maintaining strict aseptic techniques
options.B: Administering prescribed prophylactic antibiotics
options.C: Skipping hand hygiene between patients
options.D: Monitoring for subtle temperature spikes

explanation: Never skip hand hygiene! Clean hands are always a must, especially when caring for vulnerable patients who can easily catch infections.

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical concern when using connected monitoring devices?

options.A: Balancing constant safety tracking with the right to privacy
options.B: Guarantees that patient medical bills will always be cheaper
options.C: Making sure patients understand and consent to surveillance
options.D: Protecting wireless patient data from cyber security threats

explanation: Monitoring devices do not guarantee lower bills; privacy, security, and consent are the true ethical concerns. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is one major danger of poor communication between hospital departments?

options.A: Increased risk of sentinel events and medical errors
options.B: Faster patient discharge times across all units
options.C: Higher patient satisfaction ratings from families
options.D: Decreased workload for the nursing staff

explanation: That's right! When communication breaks down, critical information gets lost, which puts patient safety at serious risk.

question: Which of these nursing actions is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Screening adults for high blood pressure at a clinic
options.B: Tracing contacts of a patient with active tuberculosis
options.C: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.D: Administering routine vaccines to healthy children

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts—like giving immunizations to healthy kids.

question: A woman in labor has a fast heart rate (110 bpm) and very pale eyelids. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell her to walk around the ward to boost circulation
options.B: Check her hemoglobin level and notify the doctor right away
options.C: Give her iron pills and send her home
options.D: Rush her for a C-section without lab tests

explanation: A racing pulse plus paleness means her body is struggling. Always check labs and alert the team immediately!

question: What is the main benefit of placing a severe COVID-19 patient in the prone position (lying on their stomach)?

options.A: It improves oxygen exchange and lung expansion
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for intravenous lines
options.C: It prevents the patient from coughing during sleep
options.D: It allows the patient to feed themselves more easily

explanation: Well done! Gravity helps open up parts of the lungs that are pressed down when lying on the back, making it much easier for the patient to get oxygen.

question: What makes blunt force trauma to the abdomen so dangerous?

options.A: Permanent stiffening of the peripheral joints
options.B: Immediate infection of the superficial skin layers
options.C: Rapid development of severe seasonal allergies
options.D: Massive internal bleeding without visible external wounds

explanation: A person can look fine on the outside while bleeding heavily inside. That's why careful, hands-on nursing assessment is always key!

question: What type of health issue usually spikes during the first few hours of a sudden disaster?

options.A: Delayed seasonal allergy symptoms
options.B: Acute physical trauma and injuries
options.C: Chronic degenerative nerve disorders
options.D: Long-term nutritional deficiencies

explanation: Right after sudden events like storms or earthquakes, the most common sights are physical injuries, cuts, and fractures that need immediate care.

question: How does having a daily work schedule help a client dealing with auditory hallucinations?

options.A: It replaces the need for any psychiatric evaluation
options.B: It blocks all sound waves from entering the ears
options.C: It completely cures the brain of abnormal electrical impulses
options.D: It provides a healthy distraction from distressing symptoms

explanation: When clients are busy focusing on work tasks, they have less time to dwell on troubling internal voices. You're doing great!

question: Why is it important to test movement and feeling in the fingers or toes below a wound before stitching it?

options.A: To make the skin easier to numb with medication
options.B: To prevent the wound from becoming infected later
options.C: To see if the patient is allergic to local anesthetics
options.D: To check if nerves and blood vessels were damaged by the injury

explanation: Testing distal motor and sensory function helps catch nerve or vessel damage early, before any repair work begins. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a key way your blood helps regulate your body?

options.A: Maintaining normal body temperature
options.B: Generating electrical impulses for the heart
options.C: Synthesizing new digestive enzymes
options.D: Producing red bone marrow stem cells

explanation: Well done! Blood acts like a personal heating system, picking up heat from active muscles and sharing it around the body to keep you at a steady, safe temperature.

question: What is the main purpose of establishing a clear case definition in surveillance?

options.A: Determining the exact cost of hospital treatment for insurance claims
options.B: Speeding up the time it takes to prescribe antibiotics to a patient
options.C: Fulfilling administrative paperwork requirements without clinical value
options.D: Ensuring everyone uses the exact same criteria to identify a disease

explanation: A standard case definition ensures that health workers across different regions are counting the exact same illness criteria. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does good family nutrition directly help a patient managing HIV?

options.A: It cures any underlying opportunistic infections present
options.B: It replaces the need for daily medication intake
options.C: It guarantees an immediate increase in white blood cells
options.D: It strengthens immunity and helps process medications

explanation: Well done! Nutritious meals support overall body strength and help the system tolerate drug regimens successfully.

question: As a community health nurse, you notice several villagers showing signs of fever and yellow eyes. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Report the cluster to local public health authorities for investigation
options.B: Distribute mosquito repellent creams without informing the government
options.C: Advise villagers to wait two weeks to see if symptoms disappear
options.D: Close down all local markets and schools in the affected region

explanation: You're a star! Always report unusual clusters of disease right away so public health teams can step in and protect the whole community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h8)

question: A depressed patient says that life feels completely hopeless. What is the best, most therapeutic way to reply?

options.A: It sounds like you are carrying a very heavy burden right now. Let us talk about it.
options.B: Do not worry about it, many people feel much worse than you do.
options.C: Everything will look much brighter tomorrow once you get some sleep.
options.D: You have so many things to be grateful for, so try not to feel down.

explanation: Wonderful! Validating their feelings without dismissing them builds trust and opens the door for a truly helpful conversation.

question: What is the main purpose of using a Punnett square?

options.A: To check if a patient has an active bacterial infection
options.B: To predict the probability of an offspring inheriting a trait
options.C: To count the exact number of chromosomes in a patient
options.D: To measure the physical length of a single DNA strand

explanation: Clinicians and researchers use Punnett squares to calculate the mathematical odds of passing down specific genetic traits. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h3)

question: How should a nurse apply a prescribed cream onto a patient's forearm?

options.A: Pat it into a thick pile and cover with tight gauze
options.B: Massage it hard until the skin turns bright red
options.C: Scrub it aggressively in circles to force deep penetration
options.D: Smooth it on gently in the direction of hair growth

explanation: Gentle, smooth strokes following hair growth prevent skin irritation, hair follicle inflammation, and unnecessary friction. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h7)

question: Which three choices can a team make during the 'Act' phase of a PDSA cycle?

options.A: Adopt, adapt, or abandon
options.B: Ignore, accept, or delay
options.C: Create, distribute, or destroy
options.D: Punish, reward, or reassign

explanation: You got it! Based on what we studied, we either take the idea on (adopt), tweak it (adapt), or drop it completely (abandon).

question: Why must a nurse be careful not to confuse statistical significance with real clinical usefulness?

options.A: Clinical importance only matters if the p-value is exactly equal to zero
options.B: A tiny change in numbers can reach statistical significance in a huge study without helping patients much
options.C: Statistical programs always hide the real health outcomes from the nursing staff
options.D: Statistical significance is completely made up and has no place in modern hospital wards

explanation: If a study is massive, even a tiny, unimportant number change can look 'statistically significant' even if patients don't feel any real health benefit.

question: Which lifestyle change makes the biggest difference in preventing oral cancer?

options.A: Avoiding all dairy products in the diet
options.B: Taking daily multivitamin supplements
options.C: Using hard-bristled toothbrushes twice daily
options.D: Stopping tobacco use and limiting alcohol

explanation: Smoking, tobacco use, and heavy drinking are the main culprits behind most oral cancers.

question: What three areas does the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) assess?

options.A: Blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature
options.B: Swallowing reflex, pupil size, and skin color
options.C: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.D: Pain tolerance, mood, and cognitive memory

explanation: The GCS is a quick, reliable way to check a patient's level of consciousness by testing these three clear reactions.

question: What is the main goal of supported housing for patients on psychiatric parole?

options.A: To punish individuals who fail to follow hospital rules
options.B: To provide a safe middle ground between total hospitalization and living alone
options.C: To serve as a permanent replacement for outpatient clinics
options.D: To keep patients completely isolated from the outside community

explanation: Spot on! Supported housing gives patients the right amount of supervision and structure while letting them practice real-world living.

question: Why are omega-3 fatty acids particularly important in the diet of a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: They support the infant's brain and nervous system development
options.B: They stimulate the immediate release of oxytocin during feeding
options.C: They act as the primary source of daily energy for the mother
options.D: They prevent the mother from gaining too much postpartum weight

explanation: Omega-3 fatty acids, especially DHA passed through breast milk, play a major role in building the baby's brain and eyes. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h3)

question: What is the main job of amino acids once they enter our cells?

options.A: Synthesizing structural proteins, enzymes, and antibodies
options.B: Binding to water molecules to maintain blood pressure
options.C: Providing the bulk of resting energy during sleep
options.D: Converting directly into quick-acting glycogen stores

explanation: Fantastic! Amino acids are primarily the body's master builders—used to create tissues, enzymes, and infection-fighting antibodies rather than just burning for fuel.

question: What's the main difference between an outbreak and an epidemic?

options.A: An outbreak lasts for years whereas an epidemic lasts for days
options.B: Epidemics are caused exclusively by bacteria, never by viruses
options.C: An epidemic covers a much larger geographical area or population
options.D: Outbreaks only affect children while epidemics affect adults

explanation: Think of an outbreak as localized, while an epidemic spreads wider to affect a much bigger region or population.

question: What do we call using someone else's ideas or words without giving them proper credit?

options.A: Synthesis
options.B: Plagiarism
options.C: Citation
options.D: Paraphrasing

explanation: Plagiarism means taking another person's work or ideas and presenting them as your own without acknowledging them.

question: What personal protective equipment is a must when working in the CSSD decontamination room?

options.A: Waterproof gowns, utility gloves, and face shields
options.B: Dust masks and cotton lab coats
options.C: Sterile surgical gloves and sterile cloth gowns only
options.D: Lead aprons and radiation dosimeter badges

explanation: Decontamination staff deal with splashes of dirty water, blood, and harsh chemicals, so waterproof gear and face shields are essential to stay safe.

question: Which of these forms the foundation (Tier 1) of the MHPSS pyramid?

options.A: Running community support groups for grief
options.B: Ensuring access to food, shelter, and basic safety
options.C: Providing specialized psychiatric medications
options.D: Conducting individual trauma counseling

explanation: Spot on! Tier 1 is all about basic human survival needs like food, water, and physical safety before we can tackle deeper emotional issues.

question: A patient stops taking their prescribed tuberculosis medication because it makes them feel nauseated every morning. What kind of barrier does this represent?

options.A: Financial barrier
options.B: Language barrier
options.C: Transportation barrier
options.D: Side effect barrier

explanation: Adverse drug reactions such as nausea are common side effects that discourage patients from continuing their treatment unless managed properly. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is a rate more useful than a simple count when comparing disease frequency between a large city and a small village?

options.A: A rate only counts people who are admitted to private hospitals
options.B: A rate adjusts for differences in total population size
options.C: A simple count is always illegal to use in public health
options.D: A rate completely eliminates the need for data collection

explanation: Spot on! Because cities and villages have different numbers of people, using a rate lets us make a fair, accurate comparison. Excellent reasoning!

question: Which learning disability specifically impairs a person's ability to perform mathematical calculations?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Dysgraphia
options.C: Dyslexia
options.D: Dyscalculia

explanation: Dyscalculia is the specific neurological term for difficulties involving numbers and math concepts. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h2)

question: When you turn your palm downward to type on a phone or keyboard, what is this movement called?

options.A: Elevation
options.B: Adduction
options.C: Supination
options.D: Pronation

explanation: Brilliant! Pronation turns the palm to face backward or downward, while supination turns it upward (like holding soup).

question: What is the primary factor that food pricing reflects in a basic economic sense?

options.A: The arbitrary decisions made by local retail store owners
options.B: The total amount of money printed by the federal government
options.C: The cost to produce, transport, and sell food balanced with consumer demand
options.D: The fixed value assigned to crops by international health organizations

explanation: Food prices are fundamentally tied to the expenses involved in bringing food from the farm to the table, weighed against what buyers can pay. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h1)

question: Why is ethical data management particularly critical in nursing research?

options.A: Because it prevents frequency tables from having errors
options.B: Because computers cannot process named data without codes
options.C: Because nursing data involves sensitive personal health information
options.D: Because ethical clearance replaces the need for data cleaning

explanation: Healthcare records are deeply private, and nurses have an ethical duty to safeguard patient confidentiality throughout every step of data organization. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h8)

question: At which point in the chain of infection does patient isolation work best?

options.A: Portal of entry
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Mode of transmission
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: Brilliant! By keeping an infected patient apart and limiting contact, isolation blocks the exact pathway germs use to travel from person to person.

question: Which organ temporarily acts as a major hormone factory during pregnancy?

options.A: Gallbladder
options.B: Placenta
options.C: Adrenal gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: You got this! The placenta does way more than just pass nutrients—it actually takes over hormone production to support and protect the pregnancy.

question: A patient with a chronic blood disorder is stressed about overwhelming hospital bills and housing issues. Who should you involve in their care plan?

options.A: An intensive care physician
options.B: A surgical theatre technician
options.C: A hospital physiotherapist
options.D: A medical social worker

explanation: Social workers are absolute lifesavers when it comes to connecting families with financial aid, welfare, and community support.

question: What is the ultimate goal of Universal Health Coverage (UHC)?

options.A: Ensuring everyone gets needed health services without financial hardship
options.B: Making all hospitals in the country completely free and private
options.C: Eliminating the need for nurses and doctors in rural areas
options.D: Requiring every citizen to travel abroad for complex surgeries

explanation: UHC simply means everyone can walk into a hospital, get quality treatment, and not go broke doing it.

question: On a cumulative graph, which statistical value corresponds directly to the 50th percentile?

options.A: Mode
options.B: Median
options.C: Range
options.D: Variance

explanation: Easy peasy! The median is simply the midpoint, sitting right at the 50th percentile of your data.

question: What is the main reason a patient with acute pancreatitis is kept NPO (nothing by mouth)?

options.A: To rest the pancreas and stop the release of digestive enzymes
options.B: To prevent choking during sudden episodes of severe vomiting
options.C: To keep the bowel completely clean for diagnostic X-rays
options.D: To prepare the stomach for emergency surgical removal

explanation: Brilliant! Keeping the patient NPO means no food enters the gut, which gives the hardworking pancreas a well-deserved break so it stops producing damaging enzymes.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended nursing approach when correcting common contraceptive myths?

options.A: Validating the client's underlying concerns
options.B: Insulting the client for believing rumors
options.C: Providing clear and accurate health facts
options.D: Explaining normal physiological side effects

explanation: Insulting clients creates a hostile environment and drives them away from formal healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: What is a big benefit of linking smart bed scales directly to the Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: It reduces documentation errors and saves nursing time
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for daily physician rounds
options.C: It automatically orders dietary meal plans for the patient
options.D: It diagnoses the underlying cause of sudden weight fluctuations

explanation: Sending weight data straight to the computer means fewer manual typos and more time to spend caring for your patients.

question: A patient starts a new medicine known for causing strong receptor-blocking side effects. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Doubling the initial dose to speed up therapeutic effects
options.B: Monitoring closely for signs of excessive receptor blockade
options.C: Assuming the patient will experience complete drug tolerance
options.D: Stopping all routine laboratory blood test orders

explanation: As a caring nurse, keeping a sharp eye out for unwanted side effects helps you protect your patient and report changes early!

question: Who on the subacute care team is usually responsible for assessing nutritional needs?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Speech pathologist
options.D: Registered dietitian

explanation: Correct! Dietitians check nutritional status and plan the right meals or tube-feeding formulas to speed up healing.

question: Why should nurses involve traditional and religious leaders when starting a new community health project?

options.A: They provide free medical supplies to the clinic
options.B: Their approval builds trust and community acceptance
options.C: They are trained to audit hospital financial records
options.D: They write all official government health policies

explanation: Community leaders hold great influence. When they support a health initiative, the people are much more willing to listen and participate. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: When anticholinergic drugs block the parasympathetic nervous system, which body response naturally takes over?

options.A: Normal resting state
options.B: Fight-or-flight response
options.C: Basal metabolic state
options.D: Rest and digest response

explanation: You've got it! Blocking the 'rest and digest' system lets the sympathetic 'fight-or-flight' responses take the lead.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a primary literature source?

options.A: A dictionary definition of the medical term hypertension
options.B: A systematic review article analyzing the findings of fifty different research papers
options.C: A nursing pharmacology textbook chapter listing common drug side effects
options.D: A research report detailing the exact methods and statistical results of a clinical trial

explanation: You nailed it. A direct research report with its own methods and data is always a primary source.

question: What is the clinical name for the bulging, wide-eyed look seen in Graves' disease?

options.A: Acromegaly
options.B: Acanthosis
options.C: Exophthalmos
options.D: Hirsutism

explanation: Exophthalmos happens when the immune system causes inflammation and fluid buildup right behind the eyeballs, pushing them forward. Great word to add to your nursing vocabulary!

question: A patient eats a very salty meal. What is their body most likely to do right after?

options.A: Extracellular fluid shifts completely inside the cells
options.B: Thirst increases and the kidneys retain more water
options.C: The kidneys immediately excrete all circulating sodium
options.D: Blood pressure drops rapidly due to sudden dehydration

explanation: Exactly! High salt makes you thirsty and tells your kidneys to hold onto water to keep everything nicely diluted.

question: Why must chest compressions pause briefly when someone is giving an intracardiac injection?

options.A: To ensure the intravenous line stays securely in place
options.B: To prevent the needle from moving and tearing the heart muscle
options.C: To keep the patient from waking up during the procedure
options.D: To allow the nurse time to chart the medication administration

explanation: Safety first! CPR makes the chest bounce around, which would cause a needle inside the heart to rip the muscle tissue.

question: Why do nurses need to understand the basic chemistry of food nutrients?

options.A: It determines the physical weight and height requirements for clinical admissions
options.B: It explains how the body transforms food into cellular fuel and structural components
options.C: It allows nurses to calculate exact retail food prices for hospital kitchens
options.D: It helps nurses prescribe specific synthetic chemical medications for patients

explanation: Knowing how nutrients are built helps you understand digestion and why our bodies need a mix of different foods to stay healthy.

question: Where do most microbes found in the air come from?

options.A: Chemical reactions between sunlight and vehicle exhaust
options.B: Purely from indoor sterile laboratory equipment
options.C: They multiply and live permanently in the upper atmosphere
options.D: Soil, water, plants, and human or animal activities

explanation: Correct! Microbes aren't actually born in the sky. They get swept up from the ground, water, or living things around us.

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a patient is lacking fluid (fluid volume deficit)?

options.A: Poor skin turgor
options.B: Dry mucous membranes
options.C: Bounding peripheral pulses
options.D: Concentrated dark urine

explanation: You're doing great! Bounding pulses mean there is plenty of fluid pumping around (or too much!). Dehydration actually causes weak, thready pulses.

question: What is the main goal of tele-nursing?

options.A: Replacing all physical hospitals with apps
options.B: Manufacturing digital medical equipment
options.C: Diagnosing diseases without a doctor
options.D: Delivering nursing care using technology

explanation: Spot on! Tele-nursing simply means using tools like phones and video links to care for patients from a distance.

question: When a mistake happens, why does a systems thinker look beyond the person who made it?

options.A: To prove that the nursing staff had too many tasks to complete
options.B: To find a way to replace human workers with automated machines
options.C: To understand how the environment and processes allowed the error
options.D: To make sure the hospital avoids paying any financial penalties

explanation: Blaming an individual often hides the real structural and environmental weaknesses that let the error happen in the first place. Every nurse makes mistakes; looking at the system helps us fix the root cause so you can practice safely!

question: A patient with severe arthritis in one knee gets a direct steroid injection into the joint. What is the main benefit?

options.A: It lets the drug bypass the liver to enter the brain instantly.
options.B: It gives high drug concentration at the problem site while sparing the rest of the body.
options.C: It completely cures the underlying autoimmune disease.
options.D: It guarantees no side effects like high blood pressure.

explanation: Correct! Giving the injection right into the knee treats the local pain while keeping whole-body side effects as low as possible.

question: Why can a normal blood pressure reading sometimes be misleading in early cardiovascular shock?

options.A: Only the pulse rate matters during a cardiac crisis
options.B: Heart conditions never affect blood pressure numbers
options.C: The body's compensation keeps pressure normal before it crashes
options.D: Blood pressure cuffs are notoriously inaccurate in emergency rooms

explanation: The body works hard to keep blood pressure stable by narrowing blood vessels, meaning the patient can suddenly crash later. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h4)

question: What makes ethical choices so emotionally heavy for nurses during a major disaster?

options.A: Having to ration scarce life-saving resources among many needy patients
options.B: Having too many modern medical machines to choose from
options.C: Working in fully air-conditioned and quiet field offices
options.D: Patients having unlimited time to discuss treatment options

explanation: So true. Deciding who gets scarce life-saving care when there isn't enough to go around is one of the hardest emotional burdens a nurse can carry.

question: What is a semi-synthetic medication?

options.A: An animal hormone grown inside a bacterial cell
options.B: A natural substance that is chemically modified in a lab
options.C: A plant extract that has never been processed by humans
options.D: A drug made entirely from artificial laboratory chemicals

explanation: Semi-synthetic drugs start with a natural base (like a plant compound) which chemists then tweak in a lab to make it work even better.

question: What term describes the official power attached to a management role that lets you give orders and make decisions?

options.A: Accountability
options.B: Authority
options.C: Specialisation
options.D: Responsibility

explanation: Authority is that official backing of your position that says, 'Yes, you have the green light to direct this process and make the call.'

question: A 10-year-old child frequently misses school to nurse an ailing parent because other relatives live far away. What is happening here?

options.A: Unusually high community social participation
options.B: Excessive financial wealth
options.C: Role overload and premature parentification
options.D: Perfect balance of domestic responsibilities

explanation: When kids have to take on adult nursing duties due to lack of support, it leads to role overload and missed education.

question: Why do veteran staff members often resist changes to workplace culture?

options.A: A strong desire to take on extra administrative responsibilities
options.B: An eagerness to learn brand new hospital software programs
options.C: Excessive financial compensation for participating in committees
options.D: Fear of the unknown and attachment to established habits

explanation: You're right! People naturally feel uneasy about change when they are comfortable with familiar routines and unsure how new rules will impact them.

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done strictly by patients
options.B: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before it starts
options.C: Monitoring looks at financial costs, whereas evaluation only looks at weather patterns
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation is a formal assessment of results

explanation: Monitoring is continuous tracking to keep things on track, while evaluation measures the final outcomes and impact. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: Which specific antidote is given to protect the liver during a dangerous paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Flumazenil
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Atropine
options.D: N-acetylcysteine

explanation: N-acetylcysteine is a lifesaver here! It replenishes a vital liver chemical (glutathione) and stops paracetamol byproducts from destroying the liver tissue.

question: A nurse accidentally gets pricked by a used needle. What kind of workplace hazard is this?

options.A: Biological hazard
options.B: Physical hazard
options.C: Ergonomic hazard
options.D: Chemical hazard

explanation: Correct! Needlesticks expose you to blood and germs, making them biological hazards. Always handle sharps with care!

question: When moving an injured person, what is the most important goal to keep in mind?

options.A: Reaching the nearest hospital in the shortest possible time
options.B: Ensuring the patient's family members can ride along
options.C: Clearing the emergency scene before law enforcement arrives
options.D: Moving the patient safely without causing further injury

explanation: You've got this! Safety and protecting the patient from extra harm always come first, even before rushing to the hospital. Great nursing instincts!

question: Why are older adults at a much higher risk for dehydration?

options.A: Their bodies require zero water intake after age sixty
options.B: They sweat significantly more than younger adults
options.C: Fluid absorption is blocked completely in the stomach
options.D: They have a blunted thirst response and may not feel thirsty

explanation: The natural body mechanism that tells us we are thirsty slows down with age, so older adults often won't drink unless we gently remind and encourage them.

question: In Nigeria, what is the leading cause of vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Severe bacterial kidney disease
options.C: Untreated urinary tract infections
options.D: Prolonged obstructed labour

explanation: Great job! When labour is stuck, the baby's head presses hard against the pelvis, cutting off blood supply and causing tissue to break down. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: What determines when a wrapped sterile instrument pack officially expires and needs re-sterilization?

options.A: The exact number of days marked on the calendar
options.B: Damage, wetness, or a tear in the packaging barrier
options.C: Whether the autoclave machine was washed this week
options.D: The brand name of the paper wrap used by the hospital

explanation: Sterility is event-related; packs stay sterile indefinitely unless the protective packaging is compromised by moisture, dirt, or physical damage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: What do we call all the chemical reactions that happen inside the body?

options.A: Responsiveness
options.B: Homeostasis
options.C: Differentiation
options.D: Metabolism

explanation: Great job! Metabolism is just the word we use for all the building up and breaking down of substances happening inside your cells to keep you going. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: When a patient is put on a salt-free diet, what does it mainly cut out?

options.A: Table salt added during cooking or eating
options.B: Proteins found in red meat and poultry
options.C: Every single trace of sodium in fresh fruit
options.D: All water containing natural minerals

explanation: Great job! A salt-free diet simply means cutting out added table salt, not scrubbing away every natural trace of sodium in fresh foods.

question: What is the main purpose of a community health monitoring framework?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside nursing documentation with digital spreadsheets
options.B: To serve as a blueprint guiding data flow, collection responsibilities, and reporting schedules
options.C: To secure permanent international funding without local community input
options.D: To punish health workers who fail to meet their monthly targets

explanation: Think of a monitoring framework as your roadmap—it guides everyone on what to measure, when to report, and who is in charge.

question: How does chronic viral hepatitis usually behave differently from acute hepatitis in the early stages?

options.A: Chronic infections often cause no symptoms for many years while silently damaging the liver
options.B: Chronic infections always start with a sudden, violent fever and severe vomiting
options.C: Chronic infections resolve completely within two to four weeks without any treatment
options.D: Chronic infections only affect older adults with pre-existing kidney disease

explanation: That's why chronic strains like Hepatitis B and C can be so tricky—they can hide out in the body for years without giving any warning signs!

question: Why is relying only on medical facts without empathy not enough for a nurse?

options.A: It automatically leads to immediate legal prosecution
options.B: It prevents the nurse from writing doctors' prescriptions
options.C: It misses the human touch needed for true healing
options.D: It violates standard hospital financial guidelines

explanation: You've got this! Clinical facts alone cannot address the emotional and spiritual suffering of a sick human being. Great nursing always requires genuine compassion. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: What was the core goal of the deinstitutionalization movement?

options.A: To completely replace nurses with automated robotic systems
options.B: To transfer all psychiatric care into high-security prisons
options.C: To return mental health treatment to ancient spiritual healers
options.D: To discharge patients from large asylums into community-based care

explanation: Deinstitutionalization wanted to get patients out of lonely, isolated state asylums and back into supportive setups right inside their local neighborhoods.
